title: What If You Fell From a Plane With No Parachute?

scenes.text: What if you fell from a plane without a parachute? Speed stops climbing after fifteen seconds.
Air drag grows with speed until it balances gravity, capping a belly-down fall at about 120 miles an hour.
Real people have fallen farther. In 1972, Vesna Vulovic dropped over 33,000 feet from a broken-up airliner and lived.
In 1971, Juliane Koepcke fell about 10,000 feet, still strapped to her seat, into jungle canopy.
Airman Nicholas Alkemade fell 18,000 feet in 1944. Fir branches and deep snow broke his fall.
The speed was never the difference. Every survivor here landed on something that gave way: trees, snow or a slope.

description:
